However, in dense crop canopies, adjacent plants frequently overlap and are detected as a single object, reducing the reliability of plant-level measurements. This study presents a geometry-aware post-detection framework for resolving overlapping plant instances using standard RGB UAV imagery.
  The framework combines object detection with geometric clustering of plant components. Leaves or branches detected within each bush-level region are represented using two complementary geometric features: component centroids and radial intersection points (RIPs) derived from detected plant structures. K-means and Gaussian mixture models determine whether a detected region contains a single plant or two overlapping plants. Density filtering suppresses spurious radial intersections, and a post-pipeline ensemble combines spatial and directional geometric information.
  The framework was evaluated using UAV imagery of eggplant and tomato crops under field conditions. Centroid-based clustering achieved an F1-score of 0.89 for eggplant, while the combined centroid-RIP approach achieved the best tomato performance, with an accuracy of 0.80, precision of 1.00, and F1-score of 0.75 using K-means. Density filtering substantially improved RIP-based clustering for tomato.
  The proposed approach provides a lightweight, modular engineering solution that can be integrated with existing RGB UAV monitoring pipelines without additional depth sensors, pixel-level segmentation, three-dimensional reconstruction, or retraining of the primary bush detector. The results demonstrate that geometric reasoning applied to existing detector outputs can complement deep-learning-based object detection and improve plant-level interpretation in dense agricultural canopies.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a geometry-aware framework to resolve overlapping plant instances in RGB UAV imagery without requiring depth sensors, pixel-level segmentation, 3D reconstruction, or detector retraining. The method uses K-means and GMM clustering on geometric features (component centroids and radial intersection points) to distinguish single plants from overlapping plant pairs.
AI.motivation: Dense crop canopies cause adjacent plants to overlap when detected via UAV imagery, resulting in single detected objects that actually contain multiple plants. This reduces the reliability of plant-level measurements needed for automated crop monitoring.
AI.method: The framework combines object detection with geometric clustering of plant components. Two complementary geometric features are extracted: component centroids and radial intersection points (RIPs). K-means and Gaussian mixture models (GMM) determine whether a detected region contains one or two overlapping plants. Density filtering suppresses spurious radial intersections, and a post-pipeline ensemble combines spatial and directional geometric information. Evaluated on eggplant and tomato UAV imagery under field conditions.
AI.result: Centroid-based clustering achieved F1-score of 0.89 for eggplant. The combined centroid-RIP approach achieved best tomato performance with accuracy of 0.80, precision of 1.00, and F1-score of 0.75 using K-means. Density filtering substantially improved RIP-based clustering for tomato.
AI.conclusion: The proposed lightweight, modular approach can be integrated with existing RGB UAV monitoring pipelines without additional depth sensors, pixel-level segmentation, 3D reconstruction, or retraining of the primary detector. Geometric reasoning applied to detector outputs can complement deep learning-based object detection and improve plant-level interpretation in dense agricultural canopies.

title: PlaceReasoner-Beta: Reasoning-Driven Macro Placement and Benchmarking
summary: Automated macro placement remains a fundamental challenge in VLSI physical design. Despite decades of research, existing approaches predominantly optimize hand-crafted proxy objectives, such as estimated wirelength, and typically produce placements through one-shot numerical optimization, limiting their ability to incorporate visual layout context, codified design expertise, and downstream physical-design feedback in a unified loop. We present PlaceReasoner-Beta, a verifier-guided multi-agent framework that reformulates macro placement as a closed-loop reasoning problem rather than black-box optimization. A vision-language model (VLM) planner generates candidate placements from the floorplan image, macro specifications, and connectivity structure; a geometric verifier enforces physical legality and expert placement principles; a physical verifier refines candidates using early implementation feedback; and a post-route optimizer further improves promising layouts using final PPA. To enable reproducible evaluation, we introduce PlaceReasoner-Bench, a fully open end-to-end benchmark built from open RTL designs, EDA tools, and technology libraries. It comprises 8 designs at two aspect ratios, yielding 16 tasks with fixed floorplans and I/O assignments, so methods differ only in macro positions and orientations and are evaluated using routed PPA and DRC rather than pre-route proxies. Across the benchmark, PlaceReasoner-Beta achieves the best timing among DRC-clean methods on all square tasks, reducing post-route TNS by 61.2% at 1:1 and 53.0% at 2:1 relative to the classical baseline field. It also shortens routed wirelength on most designs despite never explicitly optimizing it, demonstrating that reasoning over spatial structure under physical-design feedback can improve end-to-end layout quality beyond proxy-objective optimization.

AI.tldr: PlaceReasoner-Beta introduces a verifier-guided multi-agent framework that reformulates VLSI macro placement as a closed-loop reasoning problem using a vision-language model planner, geometric/physical verifiers, and post-route optimizer, outperforming classical methods in timing and wirelength on a new benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing macro placement approaches predominantly optimize hand-crafted proxy objectives (e.g., estimated wirelength) through one-shot numerical optimization, limiting their ability to incorporate visual layout context, codified design expertise, and downstream physical-design feedback in a unified loop.
AI.method: PlaceReasoner-Beta uses a multi-agent framework with: (1) VLM planner generating candidate placements from floorplan images, macro specifications, and connectivity; (2) geometric verifier enforcing physical legality and expert placement principles; (3) physical verifier refining candidates using early implementation feedback; (4) post-route optimizer improving layouts using final PPA metrics.
AI.result: PlaceReasoner-Beta achieves the best timing among DRC-clean methods on all square tasks, reducing post-route TNS by 61.2% at 1:1 and 53.0% at 2:1 aspect ratios relative to classical baseline. It also shortens routed wirelength on most designs despite never explicitly optimizing wirelength.
AI.conclusion: Reasoning over spatial structure under physical-design feedback can improve end-to-end layout quality beyond proxy-objective optimization, demonstrating that the closed-loop reasoning paradigm is promising for VLSI macro placement.

title: A Lightweight Plug-in Gate for Transformer-Based Time-Series Forecasters
summary: Covariate-rich time-series forecasting requires deciding how external variables enter the target forecasting path. Existing Transformer-based forecasters usually build a covariate representation and pass it to the encoder without an explicit admission stage. This paper studies pre-encoder covariate admission as an input-side interface that regulates that representation immediately before encoder processing. We implement the interface with a lightweight representation-level pre-encoder gate that assigns sigmoid scores to representation units, and we also study a usage-regularized variant that penalizes average admission. The interface is evaluated as a plug-in module for TimeXer, Inverted Transformer (iTransformer), and Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST) under a zero-extra-tuning protocol, where each gated model inherits the corresponding baseline configuration. Experiments on the Electricity Transformer Temperature minute-level (ETTm1 and ETTm2) datasets, Traffic, Energy, and influenza-like illness (ILI) include paired forecasting comparisons, gate-placement ablation, initialization ablation, controlled covariate-admission analysis, and a variance inflation factor (VIF)-informed permutation feature importance (PFI) diagnostic case study. In the tested settings, the gate is competitive with the corresponding baselines, and the usage penalty reduces average admission scores while keeping forecasting errors close to the unpenalized TimeXer setting.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a pre-encoder covariate admission interface for Transformer-based time-series forecasting, implemented as a lightweight representation-level gate that regulates covariate representations before encoder processing. The approach is evaluated as a plug-in module across three Transformer architectures (TimeXer, iTransformer, PatchTST) on five datasets, showing competitive performance with baselines while the usage penalty variant reduces average admission scores.
AI.motivation: Existing Transformer-based forecasters build covariate representations and pass them to the encoder without an explicit admission stage. This paper seeks to address this gap by introducing a input-side interface that regulates covariate representations immediately before encoder processing, allowing better control over how external variables enter the forecasting path.
AI.method: Implemented a lightweight representation-level pre-encoder gate that assigns sigmoid scores to representation units, functioning as a plug-in module. Also studied a usage-regularized variant that penalizes average admission scores. Evaluation followed a zero-extra-tuning protocol where each gated model inherits the corresponding baseline configuration.
AI.result: The gate is competitive with corresponding baselines across tested settings. The usage penalty reduces average admission scores while keeping forecasting errors close to the unpenalized TimeXer setting. Experiments included paired forecasting comparisons, gate-placement ablation, initialization ablation, controlled covariate-admission analysis, and VIF-informed PFI diagnostic.
AI.conclusion: The pre-encoder covariate admission interface provides a lightweight and effective mechanism for regulating covariate representations in Transformer-based time-series forecasting. The approach works as a plug-in across multiple architectures and maintains competitive performance while offering better control over covariate admission through the usage penalty variant.

title: S3VD: Semantic-Guidance Spatio-Temporal Scanning for Video Deraining
summary: Heavy rainfall severely degrades outdoor videos by corrupting high-frequency details and introducing motion blur, critically undermining the reliability of visual tasks. Recently, State Space Models (SSMs), particularly Mamba, have emerged as efficient alternatives for vision tasks with their linear complexity and ability to model long-range dependencies. However, when confronted with the poor visual representations in rainy videos, Mamba still faces difficulties in preserving the integrity of 2D spatial semantics and modeling 3D spatio-temporal correlations. To break these limitations, we introduce S3VD, a Semantic-Guidance Spatio-Temporal Scanning framework for video deraining, featuring two key innovations: Multi-Scale Semantic Fusion (MSSF) Module and Spatio-Temporal Scanning Fusion (STSF) Module. The former integrates temporal semantic priors from DINOv2 to guide precise feature representation and counteract the loss of local semantic context inherent to Mamba's 1D flatten operation, enhancing robustness against extreme degradation. The latter introduces a spatio-temporal scanning mechanism and devises a Decoupled-Gating Mamba (DG-Mamba) layer, which employs two independent gates to adaptively control preceding and subsequent contextual information within the input clip, optimizing intra-frame and inter-frame correlation modeling. Experiments on video deraining benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of S3VD, achieving state-of-the-art performance with an average 0.84 dB PSNR improvement over Mamba-based baselines.

AI.tldr: S3VD is a video deraining framework that leverages State Space Models (Mamba) with semantic guidance to restore rain-corrupted videos. It introduces two novel modules: Multi-Scale Semantic Fusion (MSSF) for integrating temporal semantic priors from DINOv2, and Spatio-Temporal Scanning Fusion (STSF) with a Decoupled-Gating Mamba (DG-Mamba) for enhanced spatio-temporal correlation modeling.
AI.motivation: Heavy rainfall severely degrades outdoor videos by corrupting high-frequency details and introducing motion blur, undermining visual task reliability. Existing Mamba-based methods struggle with preserving 2D spatial semantics and modeling 3D spatio-temporal correlations when confronted with poor visual representations in rainy videos.
AI.method: The paper proposes S3VD with two key innovations: (1) Multi-Scale Semantic Fusion (MSSF) Module - integrates temporal semantic priors from DINOv2 to guide precise feature representation and counteract loss of local semantic context from Mamba's 1D flatten operation; (2) Spatio-Temporal Scanning Fusion (STSF) Module - introduces spatio-temporal scanning mechanism with a Decoupled-Gating Mamba (DG-Mamba) layer that uses two independent gates to adaptively control preceding and subsequent contextual information within input clips, optimizing intra-frame and inter-frame correlation modeling.
AI.result: Experiments on video deraining benchmarks demonstrate S3VD's superiority, achieving state-of-the-art performance with an average 0.84 dB PSNR improvement over Mamba-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: S3VD successfully addresses the limitations of Mamba in video deraining by combining semantic guidance with advanced spatio-temporal scanning, providing a robust solution for extreme weather video restoration.

title: FedeRage: Provably Convergent Agnostic Federated Learning under General Client Drift
summary: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but its performance degrades under non-IID data and stochastic client participation. Remedies built on classical Federated Averaging (FedAvg) typically presuppose that client participation probabilities are known to the server, which is rarely the case in deployed systems. We first discuss and then characterize the optimization problem that \emph{distributionally agnostic} FedAvg actually solves when participation is entirely unknown, possibly highly skewed, and of variable size across rounds: uniform aggregation is shown to minimize a well-defined stochastic objective, weighted by the participation-induced marginal, at a standard $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ rate for convex and possibly nonsmooth losses. Building on this characterization, we propose \emph{Federated Risk-Averse Averaging} (\textsc{FedeRage}), a risk-averse extension of FedAvg that embeds the \emph{Conditional Value-at-Risk} (CVaR) into the local objective within a natural distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework. \textsc{FedeRage} implicitly upweights high-loss and infrequently participating clients while adding only a \emph{single scalar per-client}, and admits an $\mathcal{O}(κ/\sqrt{T})$ rate in which the factor $κ$ is the upper bound on the ``price" of risk aversion. In contrast with aggregation-alignment schemes based on optimal transport, which require the availability distribution as an input, \textsc{FedeRage} remains agnostic to it. Several experiments on three heterogeneous benchmarks indicate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, fairness, and convergence speed.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses federated learning under unknown and skewed client participation. The authors characterize what distributionally agnostic FedAvg optimizes when participation probabilities are unknown, then propose FedeRage—a risk-averse extension using CVaR within a DRO framework that implicitly upweights high-loss and infrequent clients without requiring knowledge of the participation distribution.
AI.motivation: Current federated learning remedies assume known client participation probabilities, which rarely holds in deployed systems. The problem is that non-IID data and stochastic client participation degrade FedAvg performance, but existing solutions cannot handle unknown, skewed, and variable participation across rounds.
AI.method: The authors first analyze the stochastic objective that uniform aggregation actually minimizes under unknown participation (weighted by participation-induced marginal). They then propose FedeRage, which embeds Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) into local objectives within a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework, adding only a single scalar per client.
AI.result: The theoretical analysis shows O(1/√T) convergence rate for convex nonsmooth losses under distributionally agnostic FedAvg. FedeRage achieves O(κ/√T) rate where κ bounds the "price" of risk aversion. Experiments on three heterogeneous benchmarks show consistent improvements in accuracy, fairness, and convergence speed over state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a principled understanding of FedAvg under unknown participation and offers FedeRage as a practical solution that requires no prior knowledge of participation distribution, unlike optimal transport-based methods. The approach successfully balances performance and fairness by implicitly upweighting disadvantaged clients.

title: VeriFuse: Bounded Vision-Language Arbitration and Reason-Guided Refinement for Cooperative 3D Perception
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong scene understanding and semantic judgment across diverse tasks, but their appropriate role in cooperative perception remains unclear. Directly asking a VLM to regress 3D detections is unreliable and computationally expensive, whereas using it to select the output of a single source discards useful information from other agents. We introduce VeriFuse, a bounded arbitration framework for vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection. Each agent first produces detections independently. Around each vehicle and roadside proposal, VeriFuse generates source-conditioned geometric candidates and combines the original detections, their perturbations, and cross-source hypotheses into a unified candidate pool. A frozen VLM then chooses among three admissible actions: SELECT an adequate candidate; REFINE an existing anchor when an object is supported but all candidates are geometrically inadequate; or REJECT an unsupported infrastructure-only proposal. Experiments on the DAIR-V2X dataset show that VeriFuse achieves 0.494/0.357 cooperative 3D AP50/AP70 and limits the relative vehicle-side BEV AP50 drop under a 300 ms delay to 1.7%. Overall, VeriFuse assigns the VLM a clear and constrained role in cooperative perception: semantic reasoning resolves ambiguity among cross-agent hypotheses, while deterministic constraints determine the final 3D geometry.

AI.tldr: VeriFuse introduces a bounded arbitration framework for vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection that uses a frozen VLM to select, refine, or reject detection hypotheses from multiple agents, rather than directly regressing 3D detections.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong semantic understanding but their appropriate role in cooperative perception remains unclear. Direct VLM-based 3D detection regression is unreliable and computationally expensive, while using VLM to select a single source discards useful information from other agents. The challenge is how to leverage VLM's semantic reasoning capabilities while maintaining geometric accuracy in multi-agent cooperative perception.
AI.method: VeriFuse employs a bounded arbitration framework where: (1) Each agent produces detections independently; (2) Around each vehicle and roadside proposal, source-conditioned geometric candidates are generated; (3) Original detections, their perturbations, and cross-source hypotheses are combined into a unified candidate pool; (4) A frozen VLM then chooses among three admissible actions: SELECT an adequate candidate, REFINE an existing anchor when an object is supported but candidates are geometrically inadequate, or REJECT an unsupported infrastructure-only proposal.
AI.result: VeriFuse achieves 0.494/0.357 cooperative 3D AP50/AP70 on the DAIR-V2X dataset. It limits the relative vehicle-side BEV AP50 drop under a 300 ms delay to only 1.7%.
AI.conclusion: VeriFuse assigns the VLM a clear and constrained role in cooperative perception: semantic reasoning resolves ambiguity among cross-agent hypotheses, while deterministic constraints determine the final 3D geometry. This bounded approach successfully leverages VLM capabilities without sacrificing geometric accuracy.

title: Toward individual-level calibration in affect recognition with perceptual adjustment queries
comment: 14 pages, 13 figures. Accepted as a poster at IEEE ACII 2026
summary: Behavioral tasks measuring facial affect perception assume that identical stimuli impose equivalent perceptual difficulty across participants. However, this assumption is systematically violated by individual differences in perceptual sensitivity. Using an affective perception task as our testbed, we propose a framework to normalize for perceptual difficulty that directly estimates each participant's Just Noticeable Difference (JND) along the facial affect spectrum via cognitively lightweight perceptual adjustment queries (PAQs). We use these PAQ-inferred JNDs to re-express stimulus distances, constructing difficulty-equated tasks in perceptual space. We validate the framework in a Two-Alternative Forced-Choice (2AFC) task using two complementary behavioral measures: binary metacognitive difficulty judgments and response time variance decomposition. We find that PAQ calibration significantly equalizes perceived task difficulty at an individual level when compared to both the non-calibrated baseline and population-level Weibull calibration, while also reducing mean response time and between-subject variance in response time. These results establish PAQ as a principled and practical instrument for individualized perceptual calibration in facial affect recognition.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a perceptual calibration framework using Perceptual Adjustment Queries (PAQs) to estimate individual Just Noticeable Differences (JNDs) in facial affect recognition, enabling difficulty-equated tasks across participants.
AI.motivation: Current behavioral tasks assume identical stimuli impose equivalent perceptual difficulty across participants, but this assumption is violated by individual differences in perceptual sensitivity. There was a need for a method to normalize for these individual differences.
AI.method: The framework estimates each participant's JND along the facial affect spectrum via lightweight PAQs. These JNDs re-express stimulus distances to construct difficulty-equated tasks. Validation used a 2AFC task with two measures: binary metacognitive difficulty judgments and response time variance decomposition. Compared PAQ calibration against non-calibrated baseline and population-level Weibull calibration.
AI.result: PAQ calibration significantly equalized perceived task difficulty at the individual level compared to both baseline and Weibull calibration. It also reduced mean response time and between-subject variance in response time.
AI.conclusion: PAQ is established as a principled and practical instrument for individualized perceptual calibration in facial affect recognition, offering a cognitively lightweight solution to account for perceptual sensitivity differences.

title: Cube-Splat: High-Fidelity 360° Gaussian Splatting SLAM via Cubemap Factorization and Adjoint-Consistent Optimization
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Source code : https://github.com/guoxf304/CubeSplat
summary: Recent progress in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has enabled dense visual SLAM with pinhole cameras, yet most pipelines are not designed for panoramic imagery. We present Cube-Splat, the first panoramic GS-SLAM framework that factorizes each 360° frame into a cubemap of four fixed-orientation virtual pinhole views sharing a single optical center. By designating the front face as the primary pose state, we accumulate gradients from all faces via an adjoint mapping, thereby enabling multi-face observations to coherently update a single state while strictly preserving cross-view geometric consistency. Concurrently, our mapping module densifies and optimizes anisotropic Gaussians using aggregated cubemap rays for high-fidelity, dense reconstruction. Furthermore, to rigorously evaluate panoramic SLAM under diverse and challenging conditions, we introduce SynPano, a highly scalable, photorealistic synthetic dataset featuring parameterized complex trajectories and multi-modal ground truth. Extensive evaluations on two public benchmarks (PALVIO and OmniBlender) and our SynPano dataset, collectively encompassing both indoor and outdoor scenes, demonstrate that Cube-Splat achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in tracking accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Both the source code and the SynPano dataset are available at https://github.com/guoxf304/CubeSplat.

AI.tldr: Cube-Splat is the first panoramic Gaussian Splatting SLAM framework that factorizes 360° panoramic imagery into a cubemap of four virtual pinhole views, enabling dense visual SLAM with cross-view geometric consistency. The method also introduces SynPano, a synthetic dataset for evaluating panoramic SLAM under diverse conditions.
AI.motivation: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has enabled dense visual SLAM with pinhole cameras, existing pipelines are not designed for panoramic imagery, which is widely used in robotics and VR applications. There was a need for a GS-SLAM framework specifically optimized for 360° panoramic views.
AI.method: Cube-Splat factorizes each 360° frame into a cubemap of four fixed-orientation virtual pinhole views sharing a single optical center. The front face is designated as the primary pose state, with gradients from all faces accumulated via an adjoint mapping to enable multi-face observations to coherently update a single state while preserving cross-view geometric consistency. The mapping module densifies and optimizes anisotropic Gaussians using aggregated cubemap rays for high-fidelity dense reconstruction.
AI.result: Cube-Splat achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in tracking accuracy and reconstruction fidelity on two public benchmarks (PALVIO and OmniBlender) and the new SynPano dataset, encompassing both indoor and outdoor scenes.
AI.conclusion: Cube-Splat successfully extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to panoramic SLAM, providing a comprehensive framework with a new synthetic dataset (SynPano) for rigorous evaluation. The source code and dataset are publicly available.

title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
summary: Agentic marketplaces are emerging where AI agents with varying capabilities autonomously complete specialized tasks for buyers. A major challenge of such marketplaces is that buyers cannot easily determine which agent will perform best on their tasks. Reported benchmark scores may be difficult to verify or compare across tasks, software, and budgets. We introduce LEGIT, a credentialing protocol connecting certification, reputation, and proposed marketplace allocation. Certification binds measured quality and cost per solved task to an agent configuration, task domain, evaluation budget, and evidence through a signed record. Reputation links records of past task outcomes to the same identity, subject to the reliability of the reported feedback. Buyers and agents can verify credential records and inspect optional visual profiles. Evaluations reveal cost differences between agent configurations with similar observed task success, and show that comparisons depend on the evaluation budget. These results support binding performance measurements to the tested configuration and resource limits. A complementary analysis quantifies the deposits and fees required for reputation manipulation under a stated Sybil attack model.

AI.tldr: LEGIT is a credentialing protocol for AI agent marketplaces that binds measured quality and cost to agent configurations through certification, and links past task outcomes to reputation, helping buyers identify the best agents for their tasks.
AI.motivation: In agentic marketplaces, buyers struggle to determine which AI agent will perform best on their tasks since reported benchmark scores are difficult to verify or compare across different tasks, software, and budgets.
AI.method: The protocol binds measured quality and cost per solved task to agent configuration, task domain, evaluation budget, and evidence through signed records. Certification connects quality/cost to specific configurations, while reputation links past task outcomes to identity. The approach includes verification of credential records and optional visual profiles. Analysis quantifies deposits and fees required for Sybil attack resistance.
AI.result: Evaluations reveal cost differences between agent configurations with similar observed task success, and show that comparisons depend on the evaluation budget. A complementary analysis quantifies the deposits and fees required for reputation manipulation under a stated Sybil attack model.
AI.conclusion: The results support binding performance measurements to the tested configuration and resource limits, providing a framework for trustworthy agent credentialing in marketplace settings.

title: REFINEPPO: Learning Continuous Control Policies by Iterative Action Refinement
summary: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved strong performance across a wide range of continuous-control problems. These continuous-control policies, however, are often defined as direct mappings from an observed state to an action or action distribution, requiring a single feed-forward network to construct an optimal control decision in one pass. While effective, this formulation leaves little opportunity for the policy to reconsider or progressively improve an action once an initial prediction has been formed. In this work, we explore an alternative approach: rather than learning only to directly predict an action, can a policy learn to iteratively improve one, and can this iterative process provide advantages during policy learning? We introduce Iterative Action Refinement (IAR), an iterative action-construction method that constructs control actions through a sequence of learned residual corrections. Starting from an initial proposal, a shared refinement network repeatedly conditions on the observed state and the current action proposal, allowing each refinement step to revise the action constructed by preceding steps. The final refined proposal is then used to determine the action executed by the agent. We integrate this iterative action-construction mechanism with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), yielding REFINEPPO. We evaluate REFINEPPO across 14 benchmark control tasks, complemented by controlled ablations of refinement depth and update schedules and analyses aimed at understanding why iterative refinement is effective. Across these environments, REFINEPPO matches or exceeds the performance of standard PPO while demonstrating faster convergence on several tasks.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Iterative Action Refinement (IAR), a method where a policy learns to progressively improve actions through learned residual corrections rather than directly predicting actions in one pass. Integrated with PPO (REFINEPPO), it matches or exceeds standard PPO performance across 14 control tasks while achieving faster convergence.
AI.motivation: Standard DRL policies construct actions in a single feed-forward pass, leaving no opportunity for revision or iterative improvement. This work explores whether learning to iteratively refine actions can provide advantages during policy learning.
AI.method: Iterative Action Refinement (IAR) uses a shared refinement network that starts from an initial action proposal and repeatedly revises it by conditioning on the observed state and current action proposal. Each refinement step adds residual corrections to the previous proposal. This mechanism is integrated with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to create REFINEPPO.
AI.result: Across 14 benchmark control tasks, REFINEPPO matches or exceeds the performance of standard PPO while demonstrating faster convergence on several tasks. Controlled ablations of refinement depth and update schedules were also performed.
AI.conclusion: Iterative action refinement provides a viable alternative to direct action prediction in continuous control, offering improved convergence properties while maintaining or improving final performance. The approach allows policies to progressively improve actions rather than committing to a single prediction.

title: PrismAlign: Prior-Steered Multi-View VLM Alignment for Hallucination-Robust Table OCR
summary: Table extraction suffers from frequent structural errors and semantic hallucinations. We propose PrismAlign, a multi-VLM framework aligning diverse visual perspectives to resolve ambiguity. It integrates priors of table logic to assess output plausibility, decoupling structural alignment from cell content alignment. A Bayesian decision strategy maximizes alignment accuracy by exploiting the correlation between extraction errors and computable rule violations. Evaluated on open-source and custom VLMs, PrismAlign reduces hallucinations and achieves state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench 1.5, as well as on the table category of CC-OCR and PureDocBench.

AI.tldr: PrismAlign is a multi-VLM framework that resolves table extraction ambiguity by aligning diverse visual perspectives with Bayesian decision-making, achieving SOTA results on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Table extraction from documents suffers from frequent structural errors and semantic hallucinations, which limits the reliability of extracted information.
AI.method: PrismAlign is proposed as a multi-VLM framework that aligns diverse visual perspectives to resolve ambiguity. It integrates priors of table logic to assess output plausibility and decouples structural alignment from cell content alignment. A Bayesian decision strategy is employed to maximize alignment accuracy by exploiting the correlation between extraction errors and computable rule violations.
AI.result: PrismAlign reduces hallucinations and achieves state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench 1.5, as well as on the table category of CC-OCR and PureDocBench when evaluated on open-source and custom VLMs.
AI.conclusion: The proposed PrismAlign framework effectively addresses structural errors and semantic hallucinations in table extraction through multi-perspective alignment and Bayesian decision strategies, demonstrating superior performance across multiple benchmark datasets.

title: Offline Multimodal Large Language Models for Decision Support in Air Operations
summary: Air operations rely on complex rules, established procedures, and time-critical analysis under limited connectivity and strict security constraints. In such environments, analysts must combine written doctrine with images, often without access to external computing resources. This paper studies offline large language models as decision support tools, deployed in isolated and restricted environments to give analysts access to doctrinal knowledge that remains traceable to its original sources through natural language interaction. We describe a modular retrieval-augmented architecture suitable for operation without Internet connectivity, supporting both text and image input from technical manuals. As a first step toward evaluating this architecture, we report a pilot study with four image analysts of the Brazilian Air Force, combining (i) a doctrinal knowledge assessment based on their electronic-target identification doctrine, comparing human and proposed system performance on the same test, and (ii) a measurement of the cognitive workload involved in manually producing a reconnaissance target report (Relatório de Missão de Reconhecimento - REMIR) without AI assistance. The results show a demanding manual task, especially in terms of mental demand (6.0/7) and effort (5.0/7), while the proposed system matches the human score (8/10) and completes the assessment in 7.1 minutes (compared to a human average of 26.5 minutes), establishing a baseline for future AI-assisted evaluation. Finally, we describe a future evaluation protocol to systematically compare manual and AI-assisted workflows.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates offline large language models as decision support tools for Brazilian Air Force analysts in isolated, restricted environments. The system uses a retrieval-augmented architecture supporting text and image inputs from technical manuals. In a pilot study with 4 analysts, the system matched human performance (8/10) while being significantly faster (7.1 min vs 26.5 min), establishing a baseline for AI-assisted evaluation in air operations.
AI.motivation: Air operations require complex analysis under limited connectivity and strict security constraints. Analysts must combine written doctrine with images without access to external computing resources. This research addresses the need for AI-powered decision support that can provide traceable doctrinal knowledge in isolated, secure environments without internet connectivity.
AI.method: The researchers designed a modular retrieval-augmented architecture suitable for offline operation, supporting both text and image inputs from technical manuals. They conducted a pilot study with four Brazilian Air Force image analysts consisting of two evaluations: (i) a doctrinal knowledge assessment based on electronic-target identification doctrine, comparing human and system performance on the same test; and (ii) measurement of cognitive workload for manually producing a reconnaissance target report (REMIR) without AI assistance.
AI.result: The proposed system matched human performance with a score of 8/10 while completing the assessment in 7.1 minutes compared to the human average of 26.5 minutes. The manual task showed high cognitive workload, particularly in mental demand (6.0/7) and effort (5.0/7), indicating a demanding task for analysts.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes a baseline for future AI-assisted evaluation in air operations. Offline large language models show promise as decision support tools that can provide fast, traceable doctrinal knowledge in restricted environments. The high cognitive workload of manual tasks suggests significant potential for AI assistance in reducing analyst burden while maintaining accuracy.

title: Talk to Me, Jarvis: An Open-Source Edge-Deployable Voice Assistant Framework for Autonomous Racecars
summary: Recent advances in large language models have improved their effectiveness as back-end components for voice assistants, particularly in intent understanding and context-aware input classification. However, online-hosted models introduce network dependency and variable inference latency, limiting their suitability for time-critical autonomous driving applications. In this work, we address these issues by developing Jarvis, an offline voice assistant for high-level behavioral commands of autonomous vehicles. Its architecture integrates speech recognition and synthesis with natural language command classification into a lightweight, local framework. Jarvis core component is a text-to-command classifier, built using a domain-specific fine-tuning of the Mistral 7B model, demonstrating low-latency inference. Our experimental evaluation demonstrates that our solution outperforms larger online-hosted models, achieving 97.63 % intent recognition accuracy with an average processing latency of 1.39 s, making it well-suited for operations requiring quick response times. To support further research and fine-tuning, we provide an open-source implementation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents Jarvis, an offline voice assistant for autonomous vehicles that uses a fine-tuned Mistral 7B model for intent recognition, achieving 97.63% accuracy with 1.39s latency.
AI.motivation: Online-hosted LLMs for voice assistants introduce network dependency and variable inference latency, making them unsuitable for time-critical autonomous driving applications.
AI.method: Developed a lightweight, local framework integrating speech recognition, synthesis, and natural language command classification. Built a text-to-command classifier using domain-specific fine-tuning of the Mistral 7B model.
AI.result: Jarvis achieves 97.63% intent recognition accuracy with an average processing latency of 1.39 seconds, outperforming larger online-hosted models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed offline solution is well-suited for autonomous driving operations requiring quick response times. An open-source implementation is provided for further research and fine-tuning.

title: Field Tracking of Insects Using a Stereoscopic Event-Based Camera Setup
summary: High-speed tracking of small, fast-moving organisms in their natural environments is important to better understand their behavior and ecology. Traditional frame-based imaging suffers from motion blur due to low temporal resolution, and data storage limitations, propelling a search for more adaptive solutions. Event cameras, which capture changes in brightness at pixel level instead of entire frames, have emerged as a promising solution by increasing temporal resolution and data efficiency. Here, we demonstrate the use of event-based imaging with standard video-based processing methods by converting the asynchronous events into conventional video formats, allowing us to leverage the event camera's enhanced temporal detail to capture intricate insect flight movements and apply established image analysis techniques. Coupling this conversion process with a stereoscopic configuration provides continuous, low-latency, three-dimensional tracking of fast-moving subjects in field conditions. As a result, we substantially mitigate motion artifacts and achieve more accurate representations of animal movements. By making event-based imaging more readily applicable in natural field settings, our method support broader applications across animal behavior and ecological research, agricultural management, and other fields requiring high-fidelity object tracking in the wild.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an event-based imaging system for high-speed tracking of small, fast-moving organisms in natural environments. By converting asynchronous events from event cameras into conventional video formats and coupling this with stereoscopic configuration, the method enables continuous, low-latency 3D tracking while mitigating motion artifacts that plague traditional frame-based imaging.
AI.motivation: Traditional frame-based imaging suffers from motion blur due to low temporal resolution and data storage limitations when tracking small, fast-moving organisms in their natural environments. This constraint hinders detailed behavioral and ecological studies, necessitating more adaptive imaging solutions.
AI.method: The approach converts asynchronous events from event cameras (which capture brightness changes at pixel level) into conventional video formats, enabling the use of standard video-based processing methods. This conversion is combined with a stereoscopic configuration to provide continuous, low-latency, three-dimensional tracking of fast-moving subjects in field conditions.
AI.result: The method substantially mitigates motion artifacts and achieves more accurate representations of animal movements. Event-based imaging becomes more readily applicable in natural field settings, supporting broader applications across animal behavior research, ecological research, agricultural management, and other fields requiring high-fidelity object tracking in the wild.
AI.conclusion: Event-based imaging with standard video processing methods offers a practical solution for high-fidelity tracking of fast-moving organisms in natural environments. This approach bridges the gap between advanced event camera technology and conventional image analysis techniques, enabling broader applications in behavioral ecology, agriculture, and field robotics.

title: DENSE: Distilling Agent Trajectories into Evidence-Grounded Shortcut Trees for Self-Refinement
summary: Online agent deployments produce abundant execution traces, while task-specific verification and expert annotation are costly to scale. We study how to distill these traces into reusable feedback without post-hoc outcome labels, drawing on their evidence of local progress, recovery, and unfinished requirements. We introduce DENSE (Distilling Evidence from Nested Subtask Executions), which organizes this evidence into evidence-grounded nested shortcut trees. DENSE compresses redundant attempts, reconciles issues across levels using recovery evidence, and summarizes completed branches while expanding unresolved ones, linking reusable progress to remaining obligations. We introduce REFIT, a source-paired protocol comparing feedback from shared initial trajectories under post-hoc outcome blindness, with environments and model contexts reset for fresh attempts at the same tasks. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, DENSE achieves the highest strict pass rate among tested non-privileged feedback methods across four recipient models. Relative to initial executions, strict pass rate improves by 7.12-15.64 pp, with 19.0-43.6% fewer observed recipient tokens in reruns. GPT-5.5 ablations support combining nested subtask analysis with shortcut construction and issue reconciliation. These findings point toward agent self-refinement through evidence-grounded trajectory reuse with less reliance on external supervision.

AI.tldr: DENSE is a method for distilling execution traces from online agent deployments into reusable feedback without requiring post-hoc outcome labels. It organizes evidence into evidence-grounded nested shortcut trees, compressing redundant attempts, reconciling issues across levels, and linking reusable progress to remaining obligations. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, DENSE achieves the highest strict pass rate among non-privileged feedback methods, with 7.12-15.64 pp improvement in pass rate and 19.0-43.6% token reduction in reruns.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to scale agent feedback without costly task-specific verification and expert annotation. Online agent deployments produce abundant execution traces, but these traces lack post-hoc outcome labels, making it challenging to extract reusable feedback. The key insight is to leverage evidence of local progress, recovery, and unfinished requirements from the traces themselves.
AI.method: DENSE organizes evidence into evidence-grounded nested shortcut trees through three main processes: (1) compressing redundant attempts, (2) reconciling issues across levels using recovery evidence, and (3) summarizing completed branches while expanding unresolved ones. The evaluation uses REFIT, a source-paired protocol comparing feedback from shared initial trajectories under post-hoc outcome blindness, with environments and model contexts reset for fresh attempts.
AI.result: DENSE achieves the highest strict pass rate among tested non-privileged feedback methods across four recipient models on Terminal-Bench 2.1. Relative to initial executions, strict pass rate improves by 7.12-15.64 percentage points, with 19.0-43.6% fewer observed recipient tokens in reruns. GPT-5.5 ablations support combining nested subtask analysis with shortcut construction and issue reconciliation.
AI.conclusion: The findings point toward agent self-refinement through evidence-grounded trajectory reuse with less reliance on external supervision. This approach enables agents to improve themselves using evidence extracted from their own execution traces, without requiring external labels or extensive human annotation.

title: Signal-Centric Remote Sensing via Alternative Preprocessing and Acoustic Processing for ML-Driven Applications
comment: 7 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Published in Proc. IEEE SoutheastCon 2025, pp. 1078-1084, doi: 10.1109/SoutheastCon56624.2025.10971547
summary: The dominant method of processing sonar data is using image-based representations, requiring the preprocessing of image data on autonomous systems. We propose an alternative data processing method for remote sensing applications via the use of data in Comma-Seperated Value format. Experimentation on our alternative approach shows a reduction of processing time by 91.18%, an improvement in accurate object detection by Machine Learning, and an increase in SNR (Signal-to-noise ratio), PSNR (Peak signal-to-noise ratio), and other evaluation metrics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using CSV format instead of image-based representations for sonar data processing in remote sensing applications, achieving 91.18% faster processing time, improved ML-based object detection accuracy, and enhanced signal quality metrics.
AI.motivation: The current dominant method for processing sonar data relies on image-based representations, which requires computationally intensive preprocessing on autonomous systems. This creates a bottleneck for real-time remote sensing applications where computational resources are limited.
AI.method: The researchers propose an alternative data processing method using data in Comma-Separated Value (CSV) format instead of traditional image-based representations for sonar data processing in remote sensing applications.
AI.result: The proposed CSV-based approach demonstrated: (1) 91.18% reduction in processing time, (2) improved accuracy in machine learning-based object detection, and (3) increased performance in evaluation metrics including SNR (Signal-to-noise ratio), PSNR (Peak signal-to-noise ratio), and other metrics.
AI.conclusion: The CSV-based data processing method offers a more efficient alternative to image-based sonar data processing, significantly reducing computational overhead while improving both detection accuracy and signal quality metrics. This approach shows promise for enhancing autonomous remote sensing systems.

title: Hiding in Plain Sight: A Diffusion-based Mitigation of Geolocation Privacy Leakage in Vision-Language Models
summary: Multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex visual understanding. However, this very power introduces a critical yet underexplored privacy threat: adversaries can exploit MLRMs to precisely infer users' geographic locations from casually shared photographs, by performing structured reasoning over subtle visual cues such as architectural styles, vegetation, and lighting conditions. In this work, we present a systematic study of MLRM-driven geolocation privacy leakage. We first reveal that refusal-based safeguards are critically insufficient, as carefully crafted jailbreak prompts can raise model response rates to 100%. We further identify that existing defenses, which inject imperceptible perturbations into shared images, suffer from structural limitations intrinsic to their pixel-space optimization, resulting in degraded black-box transferability and pronounced visual artifacts. Motivated by these findings, we propose a diffusion-based framework that provides targeted, proactive defense against geolocation privacy leakage. By injecting perturbations into the latent space of a diffusion model during reverse sampling, our method operates directly on high-level semantic representations, thereby resolving the effectiveness-utility bottlenecks by construction. We further ground our optimization with GeoCLIP, a model explicitly aligned with GPS coordinates, as a surrogate to pinpoint and disrupt the geographic signals that MLRMs exploit for location inference. This targeted semantic disruption yields significantly stronger black-box transferability while preserving perceptual image quality, offering a seamless integration on social media platforms.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates privacy leakage in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models (MLRMs), where adversaries can infer users' geographic locations from shared photographs by analyzing visual cues. The authors demonstrate that existing safeguards are inadequate and propose a diffusion-based defense framework that operates in latent space using GeoCLIP to disrupt geographic signals while preserving image quality.
AI.motivation: The rapid advancement of MLRMs has created a critical yet underexplored privacy threat: adversaries can exploit these models to precisely infer users' geographic locations from casually shared photographs through structured reasoning over subtle visual cues (architectural styles, vegetation, lighting). Existing defenses based on pixel-space perturbations suffer from poor black-box transferability and visual artifacts, necessitating a more effective approach.
AI.method: The authors propose a diffusion-based framework that injects perturbations into the latent space of a diffusion model during reverse sampling. This approach operates on high-level semantic representations rather than pixel space. The optimization is grounded using GeoCLIP, a model explicitly aligned with GPS coordinates, as a surrogate to identify and disrupt the geographic signals that MLRMs exploit for location inference.
AI.result: The study reveals that refusal-based safeguards are critically insufficient, as carefully crafted jailbreak prompts can achieve 100% model response rates. The proposed diffusion-based method achieves significantly stronger black-box transferability while preserving perceptual image quality, offering seamless integration potential for social media platforms.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first systematic study of MLRM-driven geolocation privacy leakage and demonstrates that semantic-level defenses in latent space outperform traditional pixel-space approaches. The proposed framework offers a promising solution for protecting user privacy against location inference attacks while maintaining visual utility.

title: GVPO++: Group Variance Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training and On-Policy Distillation
comment: Extended version of the NeurIPS 2025 paper "GVPO: Group Variance Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Post-Training"
summary:
Post-training plays a pivotal role in enhancing the reasoning capabilities and task-specific expertise of large language models (LLMs). Despite recent advances in post-training methods, such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), their practical deployment remains impeded by training instability arising from the reliance on importance sampling.
  We introduce Group Variance Policy Optimization (GVPO), a novel post-training method that integrates the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization into its gradient weighting scheme. This formulation provides an intuitive interpretation: GVPO's gradient corresponds to the mean squared error between the central distance of implicit rewards and that of actual rewards. GVPO offers two key advantages: (1) it guarantees a unique optimal solution, exactly to the KL-constrained reward maximization objective, and (2) it enables flexible sampling distributions without requiring importance sampling.
  Beyond general post-training, we show that GVPO naturally extends to on-policy distillation (OPD). Furthermore, GVPO enables the optimization of a broad family of extended OPD objectives, providing a principled foundation for diverse objective design. By unifying theoretical guarantees with practical adaptability, GVPO establishes a new paradigm for reliable and versatile LLM post-training and on-policy distillation.

AI.tldr: GVPO (Group Variance Policy Optimization) is a novel post-training method for LLMs that integrates the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization into its gradient weighting scheme, eliminating training instability issues caused by importance sampling and enabling flexible sampling distributions.
AI.motivation: Existing post-training methods like GRPO suffer from training instability due to reliance on importance sampling, which impedes their practical deployment for enhancing LLM reasoning capabilities and task-specific expertise.
AI.method: GVPO integrates the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization into its gradient weighting scheme. The gradient corresponds to the mean squared error between the central distance of implicit rewards and actual rewards. This approach enables unique optimal solution guaranteed to the KL-constrained objective and flexible sampling without requiring importance sampling.
AI.result: GVPO offers two key advantages: (1) guarantees a unique optimal solution exactly to the KL-constrained reward maximization objective, and (2) enables flexible sampling distributions without requiring importance sampling. It also naturally extends to on-policy distillation (OPD) and enables optimization of a broad family of extended OPD objectives.
AI.conclusion: GVPO establishes a new paradigm for reliable and versatile LLM post-training and on-policy distillation by unifying theoretical guarantees with practical adaptability, providing a principled foundation for diverse objective design.

title: Layerwise Decoupling for Stable Structured Sparsification of Fully Connected Layers
summary: We propose a decoupled, layerwise method for structurally sparsifying the fully connected layers of pretrained neural networks. Rather than penalizing all layers jointly, our approach extracts shallow two-layer subnetworks, normalizes the inner weights, and applies a structured group penalty to the outer weight matrix of each block, processing layers sequentially to prune neurons and reduce the width of each layer. We prove that the constrained decoupled objective is equivalent at optimality to a specific joint penalty on the inner and outer weights, for any positively homogeneous activation, and thus admits a clean projected and proximal formulation. Our central finding is that this decoupled reformulation is more robust than coupled methods. In numerical experiments it provides a wider usable range of the regularization strength and a lower rate of catastrophic over-pruning than the tested joint baseline while maintaining comparable accuracy. We establish these properties in controlled classification and sparse-recovery studies, and examine their scope in a high-dimensional PINN stress test and in the feed-forward layers of OPT-1.3B.

AI.tldr: A decoupled, layerwise method for structurally sparsifying fully connected layers of pretrained neural networks that processes layers sequentially to prune neurons and reduce width, with provable equivalence to joint penalty methods.
AI.motivation: Current coupled methods for neural network pruning suffer from limited usable range of regularization strength and catastrophic over-pruning issues. The authors seek a more robust approach that can effectively reduce model width while maintaining accuracy.
AI.method: The method extracts shallow two-layer subnetworks, normalizes inner weights, and applies a structured group penalty to the outer weight matrix of each block. Layers are processed sequentially. For any positively homogeneous activation, the constrained decoupled objective is proven equivalent at optimality to a specific joint penalty on inner and outer weights, enabling projected and proximal formulations.
AI.result: The decoupled reformulation provides a wider usable range of regularization strength and lower rate of catastrophic over-pruning compared to joint baseline methods, while maintaining comparable accuracy. Validated in classification, sparse-recovery studies, high-dimensional PINN stress test, and feed-forward layers of OPT-1.3B.
AI.conclusion: The decoupled, layerwise approach is more robust than coupled methods for structural sparsification of neural networks, offering better practical usability and preventing excessive pruning while preserving model performance.

title: RobotEQ-Video: A Video-Centric Benchmark for Social Proactive Intelligence with World-State Taxonomy
summary: Social Proactive Intelligence (SPI) extends proactive assistance beyond task completeness to consider social appropriateness in diverse embodied scenarios. However, prior SPI research faces two key limitations. First, existing work focuses on static images, whereas dynamic videos provide crucial cues for inferring human states and needs, offering richer information than isolated images. Second, prior work often relies on free-form data collection pipelines, which fail to guarantee comprehensive coverage of diverse scenarios. To address these gaps, we introduce RobotEQ-Video, shifting the focus from image-centric to video-centric analysis. To ensure comprehensive video coverage, we construct a hierarchical world-state taxonomy organized into a four-level coarse-to-fine structure, comprising 6 domains, 20 dimensions, 142 level-1 attributes, and 816 level-2 attributes. The resulting benchmark comprises 2K+ videos with 100K+ human annotations and 16K+ labels for assessing behavior properness. Benchmark evaluation reveals that current systems remain unreliable and fall short of human performance. We further explore how world models can help tackle this task. This work advances SPI research from static images to dynamic videos and ensures more comprehensive scenario coverage during benchmarking.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces RobotEQ-Video, a video-centric benchmark for Social Proactive Intelligence (SPI) that shifts from static image analysis to dynamic video analysis. The benchmark includes a hierarchical world-state taxonomy with 6 domains, 20 dimensions, 142 level-1 attributes, and 816 level-2 attributes, comprising 2K+ videos with 100K+ human annotations and 16K+ behavior properness labels.
AI.motivation: Prior SPI research has two key limitations: 1) focuses on static images rather than dynamic videos which provide richer cues for inferring human states and needs, and 2) relies on free-form data collection pipelines that fail to guarantee comprehensive coverage of diverse scenarios.
AI.method: The authors constructed a hierarchical world-state taxonomy organized into a four-level coarse-to-fine structure to ensure comprehensive video coverage. They created a benchmark with 2K+ videos, 100K+ human annotations, and 16K+ labels for assessing behavior properness. They then evaluated current systems and explored how world models can help tackle this task.
AI.result: Benchmark evaluation reveals that current systems remain unreliable and fall short of human performance in SPI tasks when applied to video data.
AI.conclusion: This work advances SPI research from static images to dynamic videos and ensures more comprehensive scenario coverage during benchmarking, while showing that significant improvements are needed in current systems to achieve human-level performance.

title: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Safety-Oriented End-to-End Autonomous Driving
comment: The first version of this research was completed in early 2025
summary: Sparse representation formulates the environment perception for the end-to-end driving system as a set of discrete elements like objects and lane lines. This formulation meets safety risks in crowded, occluded scenes dealing with unstructured obstacles, uncertain regions, and intricate interactions. In this paper, we propose a dense representation, risk-aware occupancy, to characterize planning-relevant risks in an explicit and uniform manner. It jointly encodes global scene occupancy, map-derived traffic constraints, and future dynamic agent occupancy into a unified BEV map. The unified BEV map captures the risk evidence for trajectory planning in both spatial and temporal dimensions. We design an E2E network, ROIDrive, to realize risk-aware occupancy. It predicts risk-aware occupancy with an independent branch and injects it into planning queries for safety-oriented trajectory generation. In addition, to quantify the safety problem, we introduce RiskOcc4D-nuScenes built upon nuscenes and occ3d-nuscenes. Our risk-aware occupancy yields relative open-loop collision reductions of 52.9% under the UniAD metric and 35.0% under the ST-P3 metric on nuScenes.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a dense representation called "risk-aware occupancy" for end-to-end driving systems, replacing sparse representations (objects, lane lines) to better handle safety-critical scenarios. They introduce ROIDrive network and a new dataset RiskOcc4D-nuScenes, achieving 52.9% (UniAD) and 35.0% (ST-P3) collision reduction on nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Sparse representation for environment perception in end-to-end driving systems faces safety risks in crowded, occluded scenes with unstructured obstacles, uncertain regions, and complex interactions. Current sparse formulations (objects, lane lines) are inadequate for safety-critical scenarios.
AI.method: 1) Propose risk-aware occupancy - a dense BEV representation that jointly encodes global scene occupancy, map-derived traffic constraints, and future dynamic agent occupancy. 2) Design ROIDrive, an E2E network with an independent branch predicting risk-aware occupancy, injected into planning queries for safety-oriented trajectory generation. 3) Build RiskOcc4D-nuScenes dataset upon nuScenes and occ3d-nuscenes.
AI.result: Risk-aware occupancy achieves relative open-loop collision reductions of 52.9% under UniAD metric and 35.0% under ST-P3 metric on nuScenes.
AI.conclusion: The dense risk-aware occupancy representation successfully improves safety in end-to-end driving systems, significantly reducing collisions compared to sparse representations while capturing planning-relevant risks in both spatial and temporal dimensions.

title: EnSol: an environment-aware graph neural network for molecular solubility prediction
summary: Molecular solubility directly affects key aspects of molecular development such as reaction feasibility, formulation performance, separation efficiency, and solvent selection. However, experimental measurement across solutes, solvents, and temperatures remains costly and sparsely sampled. Existing computational models often rely on fixed-solvent assumptions, deterministic formulations, or simplified representations of solute-solvent interactions, limiting their ability to capture complex molecular interactions, continuous temperature effects, and experimental uncertainty. Here, we introduce EnSol, an environment-aware probabilistic framework for molecular solubility prediction. EnSol represents the solute and solvent as molecular graphs and learns separate representations for each before bringing them together through cross-attention to capture solute-solvent interactions. Temperature is incorporated directly into the solvent environment through feature-wise modulation, and a mixture density network predicts full solubility distributions to capture both temperature-dependent behavior and experimental uncertainty. On the independent SolProp and Leeds benchmark datasets, EnSol achieved Spearman correlations of 0.876 and 0.601, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art solubility prediction models across both benchmarks. Beyond computational benchmarking, experimental validation across chemically diverse solute-solvent pairs showed that EnSol maintained strong predictive performance and supported reliable solvent ranking, achieving a Spearman correlation of 0.715. These results show that EnSol can support reliable solubility prediction and solvent selection across diverse chemical systems while accounting for predictive uncertainty.

AI.tldr: EnSol is an environment-aware probabilistic machine learning framework for molecular solubility prediction that uses graph neural networks with cross-attention to model solute-solvent interactions, incorporates temperature via feature-wise modulation, and employs mixture density networks to capture uncertainty. It outperforms state-of-the-art models on SolProp (0.876 Spearman) and Leeds (0.601 Spearman) benchmarks, and achieves 0.715 Spearman correlation in experimental validation.
AI.motivation: Experimental solubility measurement is costly and sparsely sampled across solutes, solvents, and temperatures. Existing computational models suffer from limitations including fixed-solvent assumptions, deterministic formulations, and simplified representations of solute-solvent interactions, failing to capture complex molecular interactions, continuous temperature effects, and experimental uncertainty.
AI.method: EnSol uses molecular graph representations for both solute and solvent, learns separate representations for each, and combines them through cross-attention to capture solute-solvent interactions. Temperature is incorporated directly into the solvent environment through feature-wise modulation. A mixture density network predicts full solubility distributions to capture both temperature-dependent behavior and experimental uncertainty.
AI.result: EnSol achieved Spearman correlations of 0.876 on SolProp and 0.601 on Leeds benchmark datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art models. Experimental validation across chemically diverse solute-solvent pairs showed reliable predictive performance with 0.715 Spearman correlation and supported accurate solvent ranking.
AI.conclusion: EnSol enables reliable solubility prediction and solvent selection across diverse chemical systems while accounting for predictive uncertainty, bridging the gap between computational predictions and experimental validation.

title: JEPA Guided Diffusion: Predictive Vision-Language Conditioning for Generative Traffic Forecasting
comment: ECCV Workshop 2026, AI City Challenge 2026 Track 5
summary: Accurate traffic forecasting requires both understanding scene dynamics and synthesizing realistic future observations. Recent diffusion-based video generation models produce visually plausible predictions but require expensive end-to-end training and often entangle scene understanding with image synthesis. In this work, we propose a decoupled forecasting framework that separates future representation learning from video generation. A frozen V-JEPA encoder first extracts predictive latent representations from the observed traffic videos, capturing the underlying scene dynamics in a semantic latent space. A lightweight latent alignment module then projects these representations into the conditioning space of a frozen Cosmos diffusion module, enabling future video synthesis without retraining the large generative model. By freezing all foundation models and training only the lightweight alignment module, the proposed framework substantially reduces optimization complexity while preserving forecasting capability. Experimental results on the AI City Challenge 2026 Track 5 benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method achieved a score of 75.1297, ranking third in the competition. These results suggest that predictive world representations learned by V-JEPA can effectively guide downstream video generation, providing a practical and efficient alternative to end-to-end diffusion-based forecasting.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a decoupled traffic forecasting framework that separates future representation learning from video generation by combining a frozen V-JEPA encoder with a frozen Cosmos diffusion module, training only a lightweight latent alignment module. The method achieved a score of 75.1297, ranking third in the AI City Challenge 2026 Track 5 benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based video generation models for traffic forecasting require expensive end-to-end training and often entangle scene understanding with image synthesis, making them computationally inefficient and complex to optimize.
AI.method: The proposed framework uses a frozen V-JEPA encoder to extract predictive latent representations from observed traffic videos, capturing scene dynamics in a semantic latent space. A lightweight latent alignment module then projects these representations into the conditioning space of a frozen Cosmos diffusion module for future video synthesis, without retraining the large generative model.
AI.result: The method achieved a score of 75.1297 on the AI City Challenge 2026 Track 5 benchmark, ranking third in the competition.
AI.conclusion: Predictive world representations learned by V-JEPA can effectively guide downstream video generation, providing a practical and efficient alternative to end-to-end diffusion-based forecasting. The decoupled approach substantially reduces optimization complexity while preserving forecasting capability.

title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
comment: This version of this research was completed in early 2026
summary: Multimodal trajectory prediction improves behavioral coverage in end-to-end autonomous driving, but existing methods remain limited by sparse scene representations. Incomplete evidence leads to low-quality candidate generation and unreliable ranking among geometrically similar trajectories. On a register-based baseline, bad and poor candidates constitute 19.74% of the candidate set, while the oracle-best candidate ranks only 33.9th on average. We propose RRDrive, which introduces risk-aware occupancy as a dense, temporally aligned, and trajectory-queryable representation. Its global structure guides high-quality multimodal generation, while candidate-conditioned risk queries support fine-grained selection. We further construct RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM with automatic risk annotations. RRDrive achieves a selected-trajectory PDMS of 0.951, representing a 1.5% relative improvement over the baseline (0.937), and improves the average candidate PDMS by 7.7%. In challenging scenes, it improves candidate PDMS by 30.2% and increases the Spearman correlation among good candidates by 0.41, from 0.26 to 0.67. To move beyond this oracle setting, we further develop an external RiskOcc predictor, a perception module that estimates risk-aware occupancy directly from sensor inputs. The competitive performance validates the representation's feasibility.

AI.tldr: RRDrive introduces risk-aware occupancy as a dense, temporally aligned, and trajectory-queryable representation to improve multimodal trajectory prediction in end-to-end autonomous driving, addressing limitations of sparse scene representations that lead to low-quality candidate generation and unreliable ranking.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal trajectory prediction methods for end-to-end autonomous driving suffer from sparse scene representations, resulting in incomplete evidence that leads to low-quality candidate generation and unreliable ranking among geometrically similar trajectories. On baseline, 19.74% of candidates are bad/poor, and oracle-best candidates rank only 33.9th on average.
AI.method: RRDrive uses risk-aware occupancy (RiskOcc) as a dense representation that is temporally aligned and trajectory-queryable. Its global structure guides high-quality multimodal generation, while candidate-conditioned risk queries enable fine-grained selection. The authors also construct RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM with automatic risk annotations and develop an external RiskOcc predictor for perception.
AI.result: RRDrive achieves selected-trajectory PDMS of 0.951 (1.5% relative improvement over baseline 0.937), improves average candidate PDMS by 7.7%, and in challenging scenes improves candidate PDMS by 30.2%. Spearman correlation among good candidates increases from 0.26 to 0.67 (improvement of 0.41).
AI.conclusion: Risk-aware occupancy is a feasible and effective representation for improving trajectory prediction in autonomous driving, with the external RiskOcc predictor validating the approach's practicality for real-world deployment.

title: HMB-GAN: Hybrid Multi-Bézier GAN for Vector Shape Synthesis
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Published in the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Software (QSW)
summary: We explore the use of hybrid quantum-classical generative adversarial networks for synthesising CAD-ready vector geometries. Unlike prior work that operates in rasterised or single-Bézier domains, we introduce HMB-GAN (Hybrid Multi-Bézier GAN), an end-to-end differentiable generative framework that constructs closed shapes through stitched multi-segment Bézier representations with geometric continuity enforced by construction. We compare a quantum-enhanced generator with a classical generator within this architecture and evaluate them across point cloud distribution metrics and geometric shape statistics. Results show that despite faster convergence, a reduction in model parameter count, and slightly improved performance on point cloud metrics, the quantum generator suffers from excessive simulator overhead and thus classically-simulated evaluation suffers from hardware constraints. These results demonstrate the feasibility of modelling structured geometries through hybrid quantum architectures whilst highlighting contemporary hardware limitations.

AI.tldr: HMB-GAN is a hybrid quantum-classical generative adversarial network that synthesizes CAD-ready vector geometries using multi-segment Bézier representations with enforced geometric continuity. It represents the first end-to-end differentiable framework operating in the multi-Bézier domain rather than rasterized or single-Bézier spaces.
AI.motivation: Prior work on geometry synthesis operates in rasterized or single-Bézier domains, which are limited for CAD applications. This work aims to create closed shapes through stitched multi-segment Bézier representations that maintain geometric continuity by construction, enabling CAD-ready vector geometry generation.
AI.method: The framework uses a hybrid quantum-classical GAN architecture where a quantum-enhanced generator is compared against a classical generator. The approach constructs closed shapes through multi-segment Bézier representations with geometric continuity enforced by construction. Evaluation uses point cloud distribution metrics and geometric shape statistics.
AI.result: The quantum generator demonstrates faster convergence, reduced model parameter count, and slightly improved performance on point cloud metrics compared to the classical generator. However, it suffers from excessive simulator overhead, and classically-simulated evaluation is constrained by hardware limitations.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates the feasibility of modeling structured geometries through hybrid quantum architectures for CAD applications. However, contemporary hardware limitations (particularly simulator overhead) remain a significant barrier to practical implementation, highlighting the need for hardware advancements before quantum advantages can be fully realized in this domain.

title: AgentVidBench: A Multi-Hop Video Question Answering Benchmark for Evaluating MLLM Agents
summary: Comprehensive video understanding is crucial for advancing artificial intelligence toward the intricate dynamics of the physical world.
